observations: Identifies the northwest Rio Bravo site as an emergency launch/access area.

Describes informal parking and trails along Kelsey Road and limited access because of proposed bridge expansion; separately describes the northeast Poco Loco site as formal parking, picnic grounds and fishing access.
sources.name: City of Albuquerque Open Space — Bosque Assessment and Update Prioritization (December 2023)
sources.limits: The assessment documents the managed site and its informal/limited state, but it does not publish an exact boat launch coordinate.

observations: Describes the Rio Bravo Bridge as an access point requiring some walking to the river and mentions parking/picnic facilities on the northeast side.
Identifies the Rio Bravo Riverside Picnic Area/Poco Loco east-bank site and its path to the Paseo del Bosque Trail.
sources.name: City of Albuquerque — Enjoying the Rio Grande / Rio Grande Valley State Park
sources.limits: The general City page does not publish coordinates for the separate northwest emergency launch; route directions must distinguish the two banks and facilities.

observations: Describes the NM 500 project and states it includes recontouring an existing boat ramp.
Documents bridge alignment, construction impacts and the project footprint at Rio Bravo.
sources.name: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers — NM 500 Rio Bravo Bridge Replacement public notice (April 14, 2025)
sources.limits: The notice confirms the ramp is affected by the project, but does not give temporary public access arrangements or an as-built launch coordinate.

observations: Documents the new northwest parking lot intended to facilitate river and bosque access.
States that the new bridge alignment impacts the existing west-bank boat launch north of Rio Bravo Boulevard.
sources.name: City of Albuquerque — NM 500 Rio Bravo Bridge Replacement environmental/project attachments (2024)
sources.limits: The design materials describe planned impacts and replacement facilities, not current day-by-day access at the launch.

observations: Reports that the Rio Bravo bridge replacement construction phase is beginning and documents traffic restrictions during the current September 2026 work period.
Confirms the road work is part of the bridge replacement project over the Rio Grande.
sources.name: KOAT — Rio Bravo Bridge construction project and closures (September 14, 2026)
sources.limits: The report is about traffic restrictions; it does not say whether the boat launch or west-bank gate is open on any given day.

observations: Publishes 35.0274595846295,-106.67462218892496 as the Rio Bravo SW access GPS reference.
Describes the approach via Kelsey Road and a gate, and locates the commonly used river access northwest of the bridge.
sources.name: Quiet Waters — Middle Rio Grande public access information
sources.limits: The coordinate is a published access-area reference, not a surveyed river-entry toe; the information predates current bridge construction.

observations: Fresh candidate-centered NHD audits return complete coverage and no source issues for both affected public routes.
The access-area control classifies both shared endpoint occurrences as review; their cached connected-flowline distances remain route-specific (442 feet and 62 feet).
sources.name: USGS National Hydrography Dataset — targeted route audits
sources.limits: Flowline offsets reflect generalized river mapping and route-specific connected-network traces; they are not a survey of the boat ramp.

decision: Retain the published coordinate as the northwest-bank conditional launch/access-area anchor, distinguish it from the northeast Poco Loco site, and require confirmation that the west-bank gate, ramp and carry are open during bridge construction. Re-audit the point after the bridge project changes the site.
